newsitem.title: USA: Outboard Marine Q3 hurt as it sought deal.
newsitem.headline: Outboard Marine Q3 hurt as it sought deal.

text.p: Outboard Marine Corp said Wednesday its revenue stream in the third quarter ended June 30 was hurt by uncertainty after it announced it was exploring strategic alternatives in April.
Tthe marine engine, boat and accessories manufacturer, said this month it will be acquired by Detroit Diesel Corp .

"Our dealers, understandably, were as interested in this process as were our shareholders and, while they shared our optimism for a successful outcome of the process, exhibited an anticipated restraint in their orders during the quarter," Outboard Marine chief executive officer Harry Bowman said in a news release. He added that order flow has improved since the announcement of the Detroit Diesel deal.
Earnings also suffered as the company realigned inventories with retail demand, Bowman said.
Earlier Wednesday, the company reported a net loss of $5.1 million, or $0.25 a share in the quarter, compared to a loss of $3.6 million, or $0.18 a share, a year ago.

An adjustment to operating income was made in the fiscal third quarter to increase boat warranty reserves $8.0 million due to a change in an accounting estimate. In the prior fiscal year, the quarter ended June 30, 1996 was negatively impacted by restructuring charges of $11.9 million for an international restructuring program, the company said.
Outboard Marine shares were unchanged at 15-7/8 Wednesday.
